answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by bonding each identity to a slowly vesting stake scored against an atlas of attested work. New agents begin with only an ember of trust; they must accumulate a sustained pulse of peer-verified tasks before stake unlocks. Spawning fake identities forces the attacker to lock capital per account and wait through the vesting delay, so attack cost scales linearly while fake agents earn nothing until the pulse threshold is reached.
